nodes.title: Beta and High Gamma Oscillations in the Cortico-striatal Network Reflect Reward Certainty on a Probabilistic Reversal Learning Task
nodes.summary: Co-authored Journal of Neuroscience paper examining how beta and high-gamma activity in cortico-striatal circuits reflects reward certainty during probabilistic reversal learning.
nodes.description: A peer-reviewed NEATLABs study focused on cortico-striatal oscillations, reward certainty, local field potentials, optogenetic modulation, and reinforcement-learning behavioral models.

publication.abstract: A peer-reviewed NEATLABs study focused on cortico-striatal oscillations, reward certainty, local field potentials, optogenetic modulation, and reinforcement-learning behavioral models.
publication.summary: Co-authored Journal of Neuroscience paper examining how beta and high-gamma activity in cortico-striatal circuits reflects reward certainty during probabilistic reversal learning.
publication.myContribution: Co-author contribution/context: performed research and contributed to the NEATLABs computational and electrophysiology analysis program supporting the paper.
publication.whyItMatters: This paper anchors the newest publication chamber around reward learning, cortico-striatal dynamics, and model-based analysis of behavior.
keyFindings: Reward-evoked beta and high-gamma oscillations reflected positive reward valence and reward probability.
Beta-frequency connectivity across cortico-striatal regions correlated with behavioral performance.
Orbitofrontal beta stimulation promoted maladaptive behavior during non-target responses.

nodes.title: Cortico-striatal beta oscillations as a reward-related signal
nodes.summary: Co-authored Cognitive, Affective, & Behavioral Neuroscience paper identifying cortico-striatal beta oscillations as a reward-related electrophysiological signal.
nodes.description: A peer-reviewed open-access paper examining reward-locked beta activity during temporal discounting, with network-level LFP analysis and computational modeling of subjective value.

publication.abstract: A peer-reviewed open-access paper examining reward-locked beta activity during temporal discounting, with network-level LFP analysis and computational modeling of subjective value.
publication.summary: Co-authored Cognitive, Affective, & Behavioral Neuroscience paper identifying cortico-striatal beta oscillations as a reward-related electrophysiological signal.
publication.myContribution: Co-author contribution/context: performed research and contributed to electrophysiology and behavior analysis in the NEATLABs reward-processing program.
publication.whyItMatters: This paper connects reward value, temporal discounting, and cortico-striatal electrophysiology, strengthening the atlas thread around translational neural biomarkers.
keyFindings: Reward-locked beta power signaled reward magnitude and decayed with longer delays.
Orbitofrontal, medial prefrontal, anterior insula, ventral striatum, and amygdala electrodes showed beta-frequency reward signals.
Beta power correlated with subjective value estimates from a computational model.

nodes.title: Electrophysiological Correlates of Rodent Default-Mode Network Suppression Revealed by Large-Scale Local Field Potential Recordings
nodes.summary: Co-authored Cerebral Cortex Communications paper on large-scale LFP recordings and electrophysiological correlates of rodent default-mode network suppression.
nodes.description: A NEATLABs publication connecting large-scale local field potential recordings to default-mode network suppression in rodents and analogous task-related suppression in humans.

publication.abstract: A NEATLABs publication connecting large-scale local field potential recordings to default-mode network suppression in rodents and analogous task-related suppression in humans.
publication.summary: Co-authored Cerebral Cortex Communications paper on large-scale LFP recordings and electrophysiological correlates of rodent default-mode network suppression.
publication.myContribution: Related contribution/context: co-author from the NEATLABs program. Existing repo context specifically notes work on large-scale LFP/behavior analysis pipelines and investigation of rodent default-mode network electrophysiology.
publication.whyItMatters: It demonstrates research continuity between neural signal processing infrastructure, rodent behavior, and peer-reviewed systems neuroscience.
keyFindings: Reports electrophysiological correlates associated with rodent default-mode network suppression.
Uses large-scale LFP recordings as the core measurement context.
Identifies a shared alpha/low-beta suppression pattern in rodents and humans.

nodes.title: Chronic, Multi-Site Recordings Supported by Two Low-Cost, Stationary Probe Designs Optimized to Capture Either Single Unit or Local Field Potential Activity in Behaving Rats
nodes.summary: Co-authored Frontiers in Psychiatry methods paper describing low-cost stationary probe designs for chronic multi-site recordings in behaving rats.
nodes.description: A methods-focused NEATLABs paper about chronic multi-site recording hardware designed for single-unit or LFP activity in behaving rats.

publication.abstract: A methods-focused NEATLABs paper about chronic multi-site recording hardware designed for single-unit or LFP activity in behaving rats.
publication.summary: Co-authored Frontiers in Psychiatry methods paper describing low-cost stationary probe designs for chronic multi-site recordings in behaving rats.
publication.myContribution: Related contribution/context: co-author from the NEATLABs research program. Repo context supports Sid's broader role across experimental systems, behavioral boxes, signal processing, and publication support.
publication.whyItMatters: This paper shows the hardware/methods side of the neuroscience portfolio: building experimental systems that make long-running neural recordings more practical.
keyFindings: Presents two low-cost stationary probe designs for chronic recordings.
Targets either single-unit or local field potential activity in behaving rats.
Complements the atlas story around practical experimental neuroscience infrastructure.

nodes.title: Mapping Large-Scale Networks Associated with Action, Behavioral Inhibition and Impulsivity
nodes.summary: Co-authored eNeuro paper mapping large-scale action and inhibition networks using multisite LFP recordings in rodents and related human EEG analyses.
nodes.description: A peer-reviewed open-access study identifying delta and theta oscillatory networks associated with action, behavioral inhibition, and impulsivity across rodent LFP and human EEG data.

publication.abstract: A peer-reviewed open-access study identifying delta and theta oscillatory networks associated with action, behavioral inhibition, and impulsivity across rodent LFP and human EEG data.
publication.summary: Co-authored eNeuro paper mapping large-scale action and inhibition networks using multisite LFP recordings in rodents and related human EEG analyses.
publication.myContribution: Co-author contribution/context: designed and performed research as part of the NEATLABs team, with repo context supporting large-scale LFP and behavioral analysis infrastructure.
publication.whyItMatters: This paper is a central systems-neuroscience anchor for the atlas: distributed neural recordings, behavior, oscillatory networks, and translational rodent-human comparison.
keyFindings: Low-frequency activity was linked with action and sensory-based responses.
Theta activity in prefrontal and premotor regions was linked with inhibition.
Connectivity between motor cortex and inhibitory regions related to diminished impulsivity.

nodes.title: Open-source raspberry Pi-based operant box for translational behavioral testing in rodents
nodes.summary: Co-authored Journal of Neuroscience Methods paper describing an open-source Raspberry Pi-based operant box for translational behavioral testing in rodents.
nodes.description: A methods paper focused on low-cost behavioral testing hardware and software for rodent neuroscience experiments, designed to support scalable and electrophysiology-compatible behavioral paradigms.

publication.abstract: A methods paper focused on low-cost behavioral testing hardware and software for rodent neuroscience experiments, designed to support scalable and electrophysiology-compatible behavioral paradigms.
publication.summary: Co-authored Journal of Neuroscience Methods paper describing an open-source Raspberry Pi-based operant box for translational behavioral testing in rodents.
publication.myContribution: Co-author contribution/context: contributed to the NEATLABs experimental systems program connecting custom behavior hardware, synchronization, and neural data collection.
publication.whyItMatters: This paper captures the engineering spine behind the research: practical, open-source apparatus design for reproducible rodent behavior experiments.
keyFindings: Presents a lower-cost operant box architecture for translational rodent testing.
Supports visual/auditory paradigms and integration with neural recordings.
Makes experimental systems work visible as a research contribution.
